learning_outcomes: Differentiate between autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition.
Explain the process of photosynthesis and essential raw materials.
Understand parasitic, saprotrophic, and insectivorous plant adaptations.
Explain symbiotic relationship between algae and fungi in lichens.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Autotrophs synthesise their own food using carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight in the presence of chlorophyll.
Stomata are tiny pores on the leaf surface flanked by guard cells for gaseous exchange.
Heterotrophic plants include parasites (Cuscuta), insectivorous plants (Pitcher plant), and saprotrophs (Fungi).
Symbiosis: Organisms live together and share both shelter and nutrients (e.g., Lichens, Rhizobium in legume root nodules).

activities.title: Testing presence of starch in leaves (Photosynthesis test)
activities.aim: To prove that green leaves synthesise starch in the presence of sunlight through photosynthesis.
apparatus: Two potted plants of same kind
Bunsen burner with tripod stand and wire gauze
procedure: Keep one potted plant in dark for 72 hours and the other in bright sunlight.
Pluck a leaf from each plant and boil them in water for a few minutes to soften tissues.
Immerse the leaf in a test tube containing alcohol and place the tube in a boiling water bath until green chlorophyll is completely bleached.
Wash the decolorized leaf with cold water and place it on a petri dish.
Add 2-3 drops of dilute iodine solution onto each leaf using a dropper and observe colour change.
precautions: Never heat alcohol directly on the flame as it is highly flammable; always use a water bath.
Handle hot glassware and burner carefully with test tube holders.
activities.observations: The leaf kept in sunlight turns blue-black upon adding iodine, confirming the presence of starch. The leaf kept in the dark shows no blue-black colour change.
activities.conclusion: Sunlight is essential for green plants to carry out photosynthesis and synthesise starch.

activities.title: Growing fungi on moist bread (Saprotrophic nutrition)
activities.title_te: తేమగల రొట్టెముక్కపై బూజు పెరగడాన్ని గమనించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To observe the growth of saprotrophic fungi on moist bread.
apparatus: Petri dish or clean container with lid
Magnifying hand lens or simple microscope
procedure: Take a slice of bread and moisten it with a few drops of water.
Leave it in a warm, moist, dark corner inside a covered container for 2 to 3 days.
Observe the surface of the bread every day for the appearance of patches.
Examine the fluffy patches under a magnifying lens or microscope.
precautions: Do not touch or inhale fungal spores directly to avoid allergic respiratory reactions.
Wash hands thoroughly after handling the moldy bread.
activities.observations: Cotton-like white, green, or brown fluffy threads develop on the bread surface. Under magnification, tiny thread-like hyphae and round spore-bearing structures are seen.
activities.conclusion: Fungi secrete digestive juices on dead organic matter, convert it into liquid nutrients, and absorb them through saprotrophic nutrition.

summary_points: All organisms require food for energy, growth, and repair of damaged body parts.
Chlorophyll, sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water are essential raw materials for photosynthesis.
Leaves synthesise carbohydrates that are stored as starch.

learning_outcomes: Identify the five stages of holozoic nutrition: Ingestion, Digestion, Absorption, Assimilation, Egestion.
Describe the human alimentary canal and associated digestive glands.
Explain ruminant digestion and role of rumen and cellulose-digesting bacteria.
Understand feeding and digestion in Amoeba using pseudopodia and food vacuoles.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Human digestive system consists of alimentary canal (buccal cavity, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus) and glands (salivary glands, liver, pancreas).
Saliva contains amylase enzyme which breaks starch into simple sugars.
Stomach secretes hydrochloric acid (kills bacteria) and pepsin (digests proteins).
Liver secretes bile juice to emulsify fats; pancreas secretes pancreatic juice for proteins, carbohydrates, and fats.
Villi in small intestine increase surface area for nutrient absorption.

activities.title: Action of saliva on starch (Boiled rice test)
activities.title_te: పిండి పదార్థంపై లాలాజలం చర్యను నిరూపించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To demonstrate that salivary amylase present in human saliva digests starch into simpler sugars.
apparatus: Two clean test tubes (marked A and B)
procedure: Take one teaspoonful of boiled rice in test tube A.
Take one teaspoonful of boiled rice, chew it thoroughly for 3 to 5 minutes, and place it in test tube B.
Add 3-4 mL of water to both test tubes.
Add 2-3 drops of iodine solution to each test tube and mix gently.
Observe and compare the colour change in both test tubes.
precautions: Ensure test tubes are thoroughly washed and dry before the test.
Chew the rice well so that adequate saliva mixes with the starch.
activities.observations: Test tube A (boiled rice) turns deep blue-black with iodine. Test tube B (chewed rice with saliva) does not turn blue-black because starch is broken down into maltose sugar.
activities.conclusion: Salivary amylase breaks starch into simpler reducing sugars that do not give a positive blue-black iodine reaction.

summary_points: Animal nutrition includes nutrient requirement, mode of intake of food and its utilisation in the body.
Digestion of carbohydrates begins in buccal cavity, proteins in stomach, and fats in small intestine.

learning_outcomes: Distinguish between heat energy and temperature.
Read clinical and laboratory thermometers correctly with safety precautions.
Explain the three modes of heat transfer: Conduction, Convection, and Radiation.
Relate sea breeze and land breeze to convection currents in nature.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Temperature is a reliable measure of the hotness or coldness of an object, measured in degree Celsius (°C).
Clinical thermometer range is 35°C to 42°C (normal human body temperature is 37°C or 98.6°F) and contains a kink to prevent backflow of mercury.
Conduction: transfer of heat from hotter end to colder end in solids without actual movement of particles.
Convection: transfer of heat in fluids (liquids and gases) by the actual movement of heated particles.
Radiation: transfer of heat that does not require any material medium (e.g., solar heat reaching Earth).

activities.title: Demonstrating conduction of heat through a metal rod
activities.title_te: లోహపు కడ్డీ ద్వారా ఉష్ణ వాహకతను నిరూపించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To show that heat transfers through solid metals from the hot end to the cold end by conduction.
apparatus: An iron or aluminum flat rod (about 30 cm)
Wax and matchsticks or small iron pins
A spirit lamp or Bunsen burner
procedure: Fix small iron pins or matchsticks along the metal rod at equal intervals using melted wax drops.
Clamp one end of the metal rod horizontally on the stand.
Light the spirit lamp and heat the free unclamped end of the rod.
Watch the sequence in which the wax melts and the pins fall down.
precautions: Ensure the wax drops are identical in size and spaced uniformly.
Do not touch the hot metal rod with bare hands.
activities.observations: The pin nearest to the flame falls first, followed successively by the next pins as heat travels along the rod.
activities.conclusion: Heat travels through solid metals by conduction from the hotter region to the cooler region.

activities.title: Observing convection currents in water using potassium permanganate
activities.title_te: పొటాషియం పర్మాంగనేట్ ఉపయోగించి నీటిలో ఉష్ణ సంవహన ప్రవాహాలను గమనించడం
activities.aim: To demonstrate convection currents in water during heating.
apparatus: Potassium permanganate crystal and a straw
procedure: Fill the round-bottom flask two-thirds with clear water.
Place a single crystal of potassium permanganate gently at the bottom of the flask using a straw.
Heat the flask directly below the crystal using a slow burner flame.
Observe the movement of purple colored water streams inside the flask.
precautions: Do not disturb or shake the water while placing the crystal.
Heat gently to make the convection currents clearly visible.
activities.observations: Pinkish-purple warm water rises upwards from the bottom, and cooler colourless water from the sides sinks down to take its place, forming circular convection loops.
activities.conclusion: Liquids transfer heat by convection through the cyclic movement of heated and cooler molecules.

summary_points: Heat always flows from a body at higher temperature to a body at lower temperature.
Materials that allow heat to pass through easily are conductors; those that do not are insulators.

learning_outcomes: Identify natural and synthetic indicators (Litmus, Turmeric, China rose, Phenolphthalein).
Differentiate between acidic, basic, and neutral substances.
Explain the chemical process of neutralisation and salt formation.
Apply neutralisation in daily life (indigestion antacids, ant bite treatment, soil treatment, factory waste treatment).
theorems_and_key_concepts: Acids are sour in taste and turn blue litmus red (e.g., Acetic acid in vinegar, Citric acid in lemons, Lactic acid in curd).
Bases are bitter in taste, soapy to touch, and turn red litmus blue (e.g., Calcium hydroxide in lime water, Sodium hydroxide in soap).
Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base with evolution of heat, forming salt and water.
Natural indicators: Litmus extracted from lichens, turmeric paste (turns red in basic solution), China rose petals (turns acid dark pink/magenta, base green).

activities.title: Testing substances with natural litmus paper
activities.title_te: సహజ లిట్మస్ కాగితంతో పదార్థాలను పరీక్షించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To classify given household substances as acidic, basic, or neutral using red and blue litmus papers.
apparatus: Test samples: Lemon juice, tap water, detergent solution, baking soda solution, vinegar, lime water
procedure: Place a drop of lemon juice on a strip of red litmus paper and on blue litmus paper using a dropper.
Record any color changes observed.
Repeat the test with detergent solution, lime water, baking soda solution, and tap water.
Tabulate results into acidic (turns blue litmus red), basic (turns red litmus blue), and neutral (no effect).
precautions: Use a clean dropper for each different test sample to prevent cross-contamination.
Dry litmus strips should not be contaminated with moist fingers.
activities.observations: Lemon juice and vinegar turn blue litmus red. Detergent solution, lime water, and baking soda solution turn red litmus blue. Tap water shows no colour change on either paper.
activities.conclusion: Substances can be classified as acidic, basic, or neutral using litmus indicator.

activities.title: Neutralisation reaction between hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide
activities.title_te: హైడ్రోక్లోరిక్ ఆమ్లం మరియు సోడియం హైడ్రాక్సైడ్ మధ్య తటస్థీకరణ ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To demonstrate the neutralisation reaction between an acid and a base using phenolphthalein indicator.
apparatus: Test tube and test tube stand
procedure: Take 5 mL of dilute hydrochloric acid in a clean test tube.
Add 2-3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator; the solution remains colourless.
Add dilute sodium hydroxide solution drop-by-drop using a dropper while shaking gently.
Continue adding until a faint pink colour just appears.
Add one drop of dilute hydrochloric acid and see the pink colour disappear. Add one drop of sodium hydroxide and the pink colour reappears.
Touch the bottom of the test tube to feel the temperature change.
precautions: Handle concentrated laboratory acids and bases with extreme care under teacher supervision.
Add reagent drop-by-drop to detect the exact neutralisation endpoint.
activities.observations: When acid and base are mixed in equivalent amounts, the solution becomes neutral (pink color vanishes) and the bottom of the test tube becomes warm due to release of heat.
activities.conclusion: Acid and base cancel each other's chemical effect to produce neutral salt, water, and heat.

summary_points: Indicators show different colours in acidic and basic solutions.
Neutralisation is an exothermic reaction producing salt and water.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is neutralisation? Give one balanced chemical equation for a neutralisation reaction.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: తటస్థీకరణం అంటే ఏమిటి? ఒక తటస్థీకరణ చర్యకు తుల్య రసాయన సమీకరణాన్ని ఇవ్వండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఫినాప్తలీన్ సూచికను ఉపయోగించి విలీన హైడ్రోక్లోరిక్ ఆమ్లం మరియు సోడియం హైడ్రాక్సైడ్ తటస్థీకరణాన్ని నిరూపించే ప్రయోగాన్ని వివరించండి.

learning_outcomes: Distinguish between reversible physical changes and irreversible chemical changes.
Identify indicators of chemical reactions: gas evolution, heat/light, colour change, precipitate.
Explain rusting of iron and methods of prevention (painting, greasing, galvanisation).
Demonstrate crystallisation as a physical purification technique.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Physical change: only physical properties (shape, size, state) change; no new substance is formed (e.g., melting of ice, tearing paper).
Chemical change: one or more new substances with different chemical properties are formed (e.g., burning magnesium ribbon, rusting iron).
Rusting requires both oxygen (air) and moisture (water): 4Fe + 3O2 + 2xH2O -> 2Fe2O3.xH2O.
Galvanisation: coating iron with a protective layer of zinc to prevent rust.
Crystallisation: obtaining pure substance in crystalline form from its hot saturated solution.

activities.title: Burning a magnesium ribbon in air
activities.aim: To observe the chemical change during the burning of magnesium ribbon in air.
procedure: Clean the surface of the magnesium ribbon by rubbing with sandpaper.
Hold the ribbon with a pair of tongs over the burner flame.
Collect the white ash in a watch glass.
Mix the white ash with a small amount of distilled water in a test tube and shake well.
Test the solution with red and blue litmus papers.
precautions: Do not stare directly at the dazzling white flame of burning magnesium as it can harm eyes.
Clean ribbon thoroughly to remove protective oxide layer.
activities.observations: Magnesium burns with a brilliant dazzling white light, leaving behind a white powdery ash (magnesium oxide). The aqueous ash solution turns red litmus blue, proving it is basic.
activities.conclusion: Burning of magnesium ribbon is an irreversible chemical change forming a new basic substance (magnesium oxide).

activities.title: Reaction between copper sulphate and iron nail
activities.title_te: కాపర్ సల్ఫేట్ మరియు ఇనుప మేకు మధ్య రసాయన చర్య
activities.aim: To demonstrate chemical displacement and colour change between copper sulphate solution and an iron nail.
procedure: Dissolve a teaspoonful of copper sulphate in half a cup of water in a beaker and add a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid to get a clear blue solution.
Save a small sample of this blue solution in a test tube for comparison.
Tie a clean, rust-free iron nail with a thread and immerse it into the remaining copper sulphate solution for 30-45 minutes.
Take out the nail and compare the solution colour and nail surface with the original sample.
precautions: Clean the iron nail with sandpaper to remove grease or rust before immersion.
Handle dilute sulphuric acid with care.
activities.observations: The blue solution turns light green due to formation of iron sulphate (FeSO4). A reddish-brown coating of metallic copper is deposited on the surface of the iron nail.
activities.conclusion: A chemical displacement reaction takes place where more reactive iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.

summary_points: Changes can be broadly grouped into physical and chemical changes.
Rusting of iron causes massive economic damage and can be prevented by galvanisation.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Classify the following changes as physical or chemical: (a) Photosynthesis, (b) Dissolving sugar in water, (c) Burning of coal, (d) Melting of wax.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: కింది మార్పులను భౌతిక లేదా రసాయన మార్పులుగా వర్గీకరించండి: (a) కిరణజన్య సంయోగక్రియ, (b) నీటిలో చక్కెర కరగడం, (c) బొగ్గు మండడం, (d) మైనం కరగడం.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఎడారి ప్రాంతాల కంటే తీరప్రాంతాల్లో ఇనుప వస్తువులు త్వరగా ఎందుకు తుప్పు పడతాయో వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Describe an experiment to show the chemical reaction between copper sulphate solution and an iron nail.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: కాపర్ సల్ఫేట్ ద్రావణం మరియు ఇనుప మేకు మధ్య రసాయన చర్యను ప్రదర్శించే ప్రయోగాన్ని వివరించండి.

learning_outcomes: Differentiate between cellular respiration and breathing.
Compare aerobic respiration (with oxygen) and anaerobic respiration (without oxygen).
Explain human respiratory mechanism: inhalation, exhalation, diaphragm movement.
Describe respiration in other organisms: Earthworm (skin), Cockroach (trachea), Fish (gills), Plants (stomata and lenticels).
theorems_and_key_concepts: Cellular respiration is the process of breakdown of food in the cell with release of energy.
Aerobic respiration: breakdown of glucose using oxygen produces carbon dioxide, water, and 38 ATP energy.
Anaerobic respiration: breakdown of glucose without oxygen produces ethyl alcohol, CO2, and energy in yeast, or lactic acid in muscle cells during heavy exercise.
Breathing involves inhalation (ribs move up and out, diaphragm moves down) and exhalation (ribs move down and in, diaphragm moves up to relaxed dome shape).

activities.title: Proving that exhaled air contains carbon dioxide using lime water
activities.title_te: ఉచ్ఛ్వాస నిశ్వాసాలలో కార్బన్ డై ఆక్సైడ్ విడుదలవుతుందని నిరూపించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To demonstrate that human exhaled air contains carbon dioxide by testing with freshly prepared lime water.
apparatus: Freshly prepared clear lime water (calcium hydroxide solution)
procedure: Pour about 5 mL of clear lime water into a clean test tube.
Insert a plastic straw into the lime water.
Blow air gently through the straw into the lime water for a few minutes.
Observe the change in appearance of the lime water.
precautions: Use freshly prepared and filtered lime water; stale lime water will not show clear turbidity.
Blow gently to avoid splashing the solution outside.
activities.observations: The clear lime water turns milky and cloudy due to the reaction of carbon dioxide with calcium hydroxide forming insoluble calcium carbonate precipitate.
activities.conclusion: Exhaled air contains carbon dioxide produced during cellular respiration.

summary_points: Respiration is essential for survival; it releases energy from glucose.
Gills in fish absorb oxygen dissolved in water.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why do we often sneeze when we inhale a lot of dust-laden air?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ధూళితో కూడిన గాలిని పీల్చినప్పుడు మనకు తరచుగా తుమ్ములు ఎందుకు వస్తాయి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: వాయు సహిత మరియు అవాయు శ్వాసక్రియల మధ్య తేడాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Describe an activity to prove that carbon dioxide is released during breathing using lime water.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: సున్నపు నీటిని ఉపయోగించి శ్వాసక్రియలో కార్బన్ డై ఆక్సైడ్ విడుదలవుతుందని నిరూపించే ప్రయోగాన్ని వివరించండి.

learning_outcomes: Explain the components of blood: RBCs (haemoglobin), WBCs, Platelets, and Plasma.
Describe the structure and functioning of human heart and double circulation.
Explain the human excretory system (Kidneys, Ureters, Urinary bladder, Urethra).
Understand water and mineral transport in plants via Xylem and food transport via Phloem.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Blood is a fluid connective tissue consisting of plasma, red blood cells (carry oxygen via haemoglobin), white blood cells (fight infection), and platelets (clot blood).
Arteries carry oxygenated blood from heart to body at high pressure; veins carry deoxygenated blood to heart and have valves.
Human heart has four chambers: right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle.
Kidneys filter blood to produce urine consisting of water, urea, and other waste salts.
Vascular tissues: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals upward from roots; Phloem translocates photosynthesised food from leaves to all plant parts.

activities.title: Demonstration of water transport through Xylem using red ink
activities.title_te: ఎర్ర ఇంకు ఉపయోగించి దారువు ద్వారా నీటి రవాణాను నిరూపించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To demonstrate that water and minerals are conducted upwards through xylem vessels in plant stems.
apparatus: A tender balsam or petunia herb plant with soft stem and white flowers
procedure: Fill one-third of the beaker with water and add a few drops of red ink to make it distinctly red.
Cut the base of the tender balsam plant stem cleanly underwater with a sharp blade.
Place the cut plant stem in the colored water beaker and leave it undisturbed for 3 to 4 hours.
Observe the stem, leaf veins, and flower petals for red coloration.
Take a thin transverse section of the stem with a razor blade and examine under a hand lens.
precautions: Cut the plant stem underwater to prevent air bubbles from entering xylem vessels.
Handle the sharp blade carefully to avoid injury.
activities.observations: Red colour ascends through the stem and becomes visible in the leaf veins and white flower petals. The cross section shows that only the xylem ring is stained red.
activities.conclusion: Water and dissolved minerals travel upwards from roots through specialised xylem vascular tissues.

summary_points: Circulatory system transports nutrients, respiratory gases, and wastes.
Transpiration suction pulls water up to great heights in tall trees.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the components of blood? State one function of each component.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రక్తం యొక్క భాగాలు ఏమిటి? ప్రతి భాగం యొక్క ఒక విధిని తెలపండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మానవ విసర్జక వ్యవస్థ చక్కని పటాన్ని గీసి మూత్రపిండాలు, మూత్రనాళాలు, మూత్రాశయం, ప్రసేకం భాగాలను గుర్తించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Describe an experiment to show the upward conduction of water in plants using a balsam twig and red ink.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: బాల్సమ్ కొమ్మ మరియు ఎర్రటి ఇంకును ఉపయోగించి మొక్కలలో నీటి ఊర్ధ్వ రవాణాను నిరూపించే ప్రయోగాన్ని వివరించండి.

learning_outcomes: Differentiate between asexual and sexual reproduction in flowering plants.
Explain vegetative propagation methods (stems, roots, leaves, runners).
Understand asexual reproduction: Budding (yeast), Fragmentation (spirogyra), Spore formation (fungi/ferns).
Describe parts of a flower, pollination (self and cross), fertilization, and seed dispersal mechanisms.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Asexual reproduction produces new plants without the involvement of seeds and gametes.
Vegetative propagation: New plants produced from vegetative parts like root (sweet potato), stem (rose, potato eyes), or leaf (Bryophyllum margins).
Flowers are reproductive organs: Stamens are male parts (anther, filament) producing pollen; Pistil is female part (stigma, style, ovary) containing ovules.
Fertilisation is the fusion of male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote, which develops into an embryo inside a seed.
Seed dispersal occurs by wind (winged seeds of drumstick, maple), water (coconut), animals (Xanthium with hooks), and explosive bursts (balsam, castor).

activities.title: Dissecting and identifying parts of a bisexual flower
activities.title_te: ద్విలింగ పుష్పాన్ని విచ్ఛేదనం చేసి భాగాలను గుర్తించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To dissect a flower and identify its four floral whorls: calyx, corolla, androecium, and gynoecium.
procedure: Take a fresh Hibiscus flower and examine its outer green sepals (calyx).
Carefully remove sepals to expose bright colored petals (corolla).
Observe the staminal column bearing multiple yellow anthers on filaments.
Use a sharp blade to make a fine longitudinal slit through the staminal tube to expose the inner style and five-lobed stigma at top.
Carefully cut open the swollen ovary at the base and view the ovules inside with a hand lens.
precautions: Use a gentle hand while cutting the ovary to avoid crushing the tiny ovules.
Handle the razor blade carefully.
activities.observations: The flower contains all four essential whorls: green sepals, colored petals, stamens with pollen sacs, and a pistil with stigma, style, and ovary containing ovules.
activities.conclusion: Hibiscus is a complete bisexual flower with both male and female reproductive structures.

summary_points: Reproduction is necessary for continuity of plant species.
Ovary develops into fruit and ovules develop into seeds after fertilisation.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain what you understand by sexual reproduction and how it differs from asexual reproduction.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: లైంగిక ప్రత్యుత్పత్తి అంటే ఏమిటో వివరించండి మరియు అది అలైంగిక ప్రత్యుత్పత్తి నుండి ఎలా భిన్నంగా ఉంటుందో తెలపండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Describe the different methods of asexual reproduction with suitable examples.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: తగిన ఉదాహరణలతో అలైంగిక ప్రత్యుత్పత్తి యొక్క వివిధ పద్ధతులను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Draw a neat, labeled diagram of the reproductive parts of a flower (Stamen and Pistil).
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: పుష్పం యొక్క ప్రత్యుత్పత్తి భాగాల (కేసరం మరియు అండకోశం) చక్కని పటాన్ని గీసి భాగాలు గుర్తించండి.

learning_outcomes: Classify motion as rectilinear, circular, or periodic.
Define speed and calculate speed using distance and time measurements.
Explain oscillatory motion and measure time period of a simple pendulum.
Construct and interpret distance-time graphs for uniform and non-uniform motion.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Motion is a change in position of an object with time.
Speed is the distance covered by an object in a unit time. SI unit is metre per second (m/s), practical unit km/h.
Uniform motion: An object moving along a straight line with a constant speed.
Non-uniform motion: An object moving along a straight line with changing speed.
Simple pendulum consists of a small metallic bob suspended by a thread; its motion back and forth about mean position is periodic / oscillatory.
Time taken to complete one full oscillation is called its time period, which depends only on length of pendulum.

activities.title: Measuring the time period of a simple pendulum
activities.title_te: లాలకం యొక్క డోలనావర్తన కాలాన్ని కొలిచే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To set up a simple pendulum and determine its time period for 20 oscillations.
procedure: Tie the thread to the bob and clamp the other end firmly to the stand so that length from suspension point to centre of bob is 100 cm.
Draw a straight reference chalk line on the floor directly below the bob at rest (mean position O).
Displace the bob slightly to one side (say position A, about 5 cm from mean position) and release gently without pushing.
Start the stopwatch when the bob crosses the mean position O going in a particular direction.
Count 20 full oscillations (O -> A -> B -> O is one oscillation) and stop the watch.
Repeat the measurement 3 times, calculate average time for 20 oscillations, and divide by 20 to get time period T.
precautions: Do not displace the bob by a large angle (keep displacement under 10 degrees).
Ensure the bob moves in a single plane without spinning or wobbling.
activities.observations: For a pendulum of length 100 cm, 20 oscillations take approximately 40 seconds, giving a constant time period of T = 2.0 seconds.
activities.conclusion: A simple pendulum of given length has a nearly constant time period independent of small changes in initial displacement.

summary_points: Periodic events are used for measuring time.
Distance-time graph for uniform speed is a straight sloping line.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: A simple pendulum takes 32 s to complete 20 oscillations. What is the time period of the pendulum?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఒక సరళ లాలకం 20 డోలనాలను పూర్తి చేయడానికి 32 సెకన్లు తీసుకుంటుంది. లాలకం యొక్క డోలనావర్తన కాలం ఎంత?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: The distance between two stations is 240 km. A train takes 4 hours to cover this distance. Calculate the speed of the train in km/h and m/s.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రెండు స్టేషన్ల మధ్య దూరం 240 కి.మీ. ఒక రైలు ఈ దూరాన్ని ప్రయాణించడానికి 4 గంటల సమయం తీసుకుంటుంది. రైలు వేగాన్ని కి.మీ/గం మరియు మీ/సె లలో లెక్కించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Draw the distance-time graph for: (a) a car moving with a constant speed, (b) a car parked on a side road.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: కింది పరిస్థితులకు దూర-కాల గ్రాఫ్‌లను గీయండి: (a) స్థిర వేగంతో కదులుతున్న కారు, (b) రోడ్డు పక్కన ఆపి ఉంచిన కారు.

learning_outcomes: Draw standard circuit symbols for electric cell, battery, bulb, switch, and connecting wires.
Explain the heating effect of electric current and its applications (electric heater, fuse, geyser).
Understand how electric fuse and miniature circuit breakers (MCBs) protect electrical appliances.
Explain the magnetic effect of electric current and construct an electromagnet.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Heating effect of electric current: When electric current flows through a high-resistance wire (like nichrome), the wire gets hot.
Electric fuse is a safety device containing a low-melting-point wire that melts and breaks the circuit when excessive current flows.
Hans Christian Oersted discovered that an electric current flowing through a wire produces a magnetic field around it, deflecting a nearby compass needle.
Electromagnet is a temporary magnet made by coiling an insulated wire around an iron core and passing electric current; its magnetism disappears when current is turned off.
key_formulas_and_equations: H = I^2 R t \quad (\text{Joule's Heating Law: Heat generated is proportional to } I^2, R, \text{ and } t)
\text{Battery} = \text{Combination of two or more cells in series (+ to - terminal)}

activities.title: Demonstrating heating effect of electric current using nichrome wire
activities.title_te: నైక్రోమ్ తీగను ఉపయోగించి విద్యుత్ ఉష్ణ ప్రభావాన్ని నిరూపించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To observe that heat is generated when an electric current flows through a nichrome wire.
apparatus: About 10 cm piece of nichrome wire (from an old heater coil)
Two iron nails fixed on a wooden board
One 1.5 V dry cell in a holder
procedure: Tie the nichrome wire between the two iron nails fixed on the wooden board.
Connect the nails to an electric cell and a switch in series using copper connecting wires.
Touch the nichrome wire gently before closing the switch (it is cold).
Close the switch to turn the circuit ON for 10-15 seconds.
Touch the nichrome wire very briefly with a fingertip.
Open the switch to turn the circuit OFF and touch the wire again after a few seconds.
precautions: Do not hold the nichrome wire for a long time as it can become burning hot and cause blisters.
Do not leave the switch ON for long periods to avoid draining the cell.
activities.observations: The nichrome wire becomes noticeably hot when current flows through it and cools down immediately after the current is switched off.
activities.conclusion: Electric current produces a heating effect in conductors having resistance.

activities.title: Making an electromagnet using an iron nail and insulated copper wire
activities.title_te: ఇనుప మేకు మరియు రాగి తీగతో విద్యుదయస్కాంతాన్ని తయారుచేసే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To make an electromagnet and verify its magnetic effect on steel paper clips.
apparatus: About 75 cm long insulated flexible copper wire
Electric cell (1.5 V) in a holder
Small steel paper pins or paper clips
procedure: Wind the insulated wire tightly around the iron nail in the form of a coil.
Connect the free stripped ends of the wire to an electric cell through a switch.
Place a few steel paper pins near the tip of the nail.
Turn the switch ON and observe the pins.
Turn the switch OFF and observe what happens to the pins.
precautions: Strip the insulation from the wire ends before connecting to cell terminals.
Do not keep the switch ON for more than a few seconds at a time.
activities.observations: When the current is switched ON, the pins cling to the tip of the nail. When switched OFF, the pins fall off instantly.
activities.conclusion: A current-carrying coil wound around an iron nail acts as an electromagnet, acquiring temporary magnetism only as long as current flows.

summary_points: Circuit symbols provide convenient representation of electrical components.
Electric bells, cranes, and electric motors use powerful electromagnets.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain how an electric fuse works to prevent electrical fires and damage to appliances.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: విద్యుత్ ప్రమాదాలు మరియు పరికరాలు పాడవకుండా విద్యుత్ ఫ్యూజ్ ఎలా పనిచేస్తుందో వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Describe an activity to make an electromagnet using an iron nail, insulated wire, and a cell.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఇనుప మేకు, ఇన్సులేటెడ్ వైర్ మరియు బ్యాటరీని ఉపయోగించి విద్యుదయస్కాంతాన్ని తయారుచేసే ప్రయోగాన్ని వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Draw the circuit symbols for: (a) electric cell, (b) bulb, (c) switch in 'ON' position, (d) battery of two cells.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: కింది వాటికి విద్యుత్ వలయ సంకేతాలను గీయండి: (a) విద్యుత్ ఘటం, (b) బల్బ్, (c) 'ON' స్థితిలో ఉన్న స్విచ్, (d) రెండు ఘటాల బ్యాటరీ.

learning_outcomes: Verify rectilinear propagation of light (light travels along a straight line).
State laws of reflection and describe image characteristics in a plane mirror.
Distinguish between real and virtual images.
Explain image formation by spherical mirrors (concave and convex) and spherical lenses.
Explain dispersion of white light into seven colours (VIBGYOR) using a glass prism.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Rectilinear propagation: Light travels along straight lines; when obstructed by opaque objects, shadows are formed.
Reflection: Bouncing back of light from a polished shining surface. Laws of reflection: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection (\angle i = \angle r).
Plane mirror image is virtual, erect, of same size as object, laterally inverted, and formed at same distance behind the mirror.
Concave mirror: Can form real and inverted image (used by dentists and in headlights); Convex mirror: Always forms virtual, erect, and diminished image (used as side view rear mirrors in vehicles).
White light consists of seven colors: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red (VIBGYOR), demonstrated by Isaac Newton using glass prism and Newton's disc.
key_formulas_and_equations: \angle i = \angle r \quad (\text{Law of Reflection: Angle of Incidence = Angle of Reflection})

activities.title: Demonstrating rectilinear propagation of light using bent rubber tube
activities.aim: To show that light travels along straight lines and cannot bend around corners.
apparatus: A lighted candle placed on a table
A straight hollow plastic or rubber pipe (about 30 cm)
procedure: Place a lighted candle on a table in a dark room.
Look at the candle flame through the straight pipe with one eye; the flame is clearly visible.
Now bend the pipe slightly in the middle and look at the flame again.
Note down whether the flame can still be seen.
precautions: Do not bring the rubber tube too close to the hot flame.
Ensure the pipe is completely straight during the first observation.
activities.observations: The candle flame is clearly visible through the straight pipe, but completely disappears when the pipe is bent.
activities.conclusion: Light travels only along straight paths (rectilinear propagation).

activities.title: Dispersion of white light through a glass prism
activities.title_te: గాజు పట్టకం ద్వారా కాంతి విక్షేపణ ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To demonstrate that white sunlight consists of seven spectrum colors using a glass prism.
apparatus: White screen or white sheet of card paper
Darkened room with a small pinhole in the window for sunlight beam
procedure: Direct a narrow beam of sunlight through the pinhole onto one face of the glass prism.
Turn the prism until the refracted light emergent from the other face falls on the white screen.
Observe the colored band appearing on the screen.
precautions: The light beam must be very narrow to avoid overlapping spectrum bands.
The room should be dark for high contrast.
activities.observations: A band of seven distinct colors appears on the screen in the sequence: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red (VIBGYOR).
activities.conclusion: White light is a mixture of seven colors, which bend at different angles when passing through a prism due to dispersion.

summary_points: A surface that reflects light can change the direction of light.
Convex lens can focus sunlight to burn paper (converging lens).

learning_outcomes: Understand forest stratification: Canopy, Understorey, Shrub layer, Forest floor.
Explain food chains and food webs in forest ecosystems.
Describe the role of decomposers (microorganisms) in recycling nutrients and producing humus.
Appreciate forests as green lungs and water purifying systems.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Canopy: The uppermost branches and leaves of tall trees that form a continuous roof-like cover over the forest.
Understorey: Different horizontal layers formed by crowns of trees of varying heights below the canopy.
Food chain: Sequence of energy transfer from producers (green plants) to primary consumers (herbivores) to secondary/tertiary consumers (carnivores).
Decomposers: Microorganisms that convert dead plants and animal tissues into dark, nutrient-rich organic matter called humus.
Forests act as 'green lungs' by supplying oxygen and absorbing carbon dioxide, and help maintain water table through transpiration and percolation.

activities.title: Observing the forest floor and humus in decaying organic matter
activities.title_te: అటవీ నేల మరియు కుళ్ళిన సేంద్రీయ పదార్థంలో హ్యూమస్ ను పరిశీలించే ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To examine forest soil layers and verify the presence of dark nutrient-rich humus formed by decomposers.
apparatus: Sample of decaying leaf litter from woods or garden corner
procedure: Collect a handful of topsoil rich with decaying fallen leaves and twigs.
Spread the sample on a sheet of white paper and examine under a magnifying lens.
Put 50 g of the soil sample into a glass beaker and fill with water.
Stir vigorously with a glass rod and allow it to stand undisturbed for 30 minutes.
Observe the distinct settled layers.
precautions: Do not touch sharp broken glass or thorny plant material in wild soil.
Wash hands after handling soil samples.
activities.observations: Soil separates into gravel at bottom, sand, fine clay, and a floating dark top layer of partially decomposed organic matter (humus).
activities.conclusion: Decomposers break down dead plant matter into humus, which enriches soil fertility.

summary_points: Forests protect soil from erosion through tree roots.
Deforestation leads to global warming, floods, and destruction of biodiversity.

learning_outcomes: Understand sewage as liquid waste carrying dissolved and suspended contaminants.
Trace the steps in a modern Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP).
Distinguish physical, biological, and chemical wastewater treatment methods.
Adopt better sanitation practices to minimise domestic wastewater pollution.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Sewage is complex wastewater containing human excreta, industrial wastes, organic impurities (oils, urea, pesticides), inorganic impurities (nitrates, phosphates, metals), and pathogenic bacteria.

Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) stages: (1) Bar screens remove large solid objects (rags, plastics, cans); (2) Grit and sand removal tank; (3) Sedimentation/Clarifier tank (settled solids form sludge; skimmer removes floatable oil and grease); (4) Aeration tank (aerobic bacteria digest organic matter); (5) Secondary clarifier (activated sludge settles).
Disinfection of treated water using Chlorine tablets or Ozone before discharge into rivers.
Alternative low-cost onsite sewage disposal systems: Septic tanks, biogas plants, vermi-processing toilets.

activities.title: Model wastewater filtration using sand, gravel, and charcoal
activities.title_te: ఇసుక, గ్రావెల్ మరియు బొగ్గును ఉపయోగించి మురుగునీటి శుద్ధి నమూనా ప్రయోగం
activities.aim: To construct a homemade physical filtration model to clean turbid contaminated water.
apparatus: Clean sand, fine gravel, coarse gravel, and powdered activated charcoal
Sample of dirty water (mixed with mud, detergent, and tea leaves)
procedure: Cut the plastic bottle in half to use the inverted top half as a funnel inside the lower half.
Place a cotton plug at the neck of the funnel.
Add a layer of powdered charcoal, followed by a layer of fine sand, and top it with a layer of coarse gravel.
Pour the dirty turbid water sample gently into the filter.
Observe the clarity of the water dripping into the bottom beaker.
precautions: Pour the dirty water slowly so that layers are not disturbed.
Remember that filtered water is not potable until disinfected with chlorine.
activities.observations: The turbid, foul water passes through the layers, and the filtered water collected below is clear and odourless as suspended impurities and bad smells are absorbed.
activities.conclusion: Physical filtration using sand, gravel, and charcoal effectively removes suspended impurities from wastewater.

summary_points: Clean water is a basic necessity; treating wastewater protects water bodies.
Do not dump cooking oil, paints, or medicines down drains.
